title: Stream interrupt recovery heuristics and ephemeral cache sanitization
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
When clients disconnect or hit network timeouts mid-generation our runtime currently leaves partial state in several places: ephemeral generation buffers, per-generation KV cache prefixes, and leases recorded in the generation manager. Leftover state causes two problems: (1) wasted memory and background CPU while the runtime retains orphaned KV and buffers, and (2) inconsistent resume behavior when clients attempt to reconnect or resume using a stale token.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic cleanup for partial/aborted generations (bounded TTL and safe GC).
- Allow controlled client resume within a configurable window using resume tokens and a lease reconciliation process.
- Implement backpressure-aware flow control that bounds per-client queued tokens and prevents the server from accumulating unbounded state when a client stalls.
- Expose metrics and alerts so we can detect regression and tune heuristics.

Scope and non-goals:
- This ticket handles server-side heuristics, lease reconciliation, and KV/buffer GC. Client SDK changes will be a follow-up but minimal fields (heartbeat/resume_token) will be added to the API. We will not rework the entire streaming protocol or the function-calling control plane in this ticket.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Generation lease + state machine: introduce a per-generation lease with three states (ACTIVE, STALE, ORPHANED). Leases are refreshed by client heartbeats (stream keepalive). If no heartbeat before lease TTL, generation moves to STALE and enters a 2-phase GC window.
2) Resume tokens: when a generation is interrupted, we return an opaque resume_token that encodes generation id + lease expiry. Resume succeeds only while generation is in STALE state and before GC. Resume requests must present a heartbeat and will acquire a new lease.
3) Ephemeral KV sanitization: add a background kv-sweep worker that deletes prefixes associated with ORPHANED generations after validation passes (two-phase: mark-to-delete then purge). This prevents accidental deletion during concurrent reconciliation.
4) Backpressure budget: per-connection token credits (default credits=8) and a server-side inflight queue limit. If a client stops consuming, we stop pulling from model execution queue after credits exhausted and return a throttled status (transient) to caller or drop oldest queued chunks if configured as best-effort.
5) Safe GC: implement a tombstone + audit log for GC events and an override for customer-dedicated deployments to extend TTLs.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Two-phase GC increases complexity but is necessary to avoid racey deletes in high-throughput multi-worker setups.
- Keeping a short default TTL (30s active + 300s STALE window) minimizes memory but may reduce resume success for slow clients; we'll introduce config knobs per-customer.
- Limiting per-connection credits may increase user-observed throttling on pathological clients; metrics and adjustable defaults mitigate risk.
acceptance_criteria: Orphaned generation count in metrics reduced by >=90% compared to current baseline within 24h of rollout (metric: streaming.orphaned_generations)
Resume success rate for clients attempting resume within configured STALE window >= 99% (metric: streaming.resume_success_rate)
KV cache reclaimed for ORPHANED generations within GC window; kvcache.orphan_bytes declines to near-zero for test workload within TTL
No P95 latency regression >5% on normal streaming workload at canary traffic levels
Feature flag for safe rollout and on/off kill switch exists and functions without requiring restarts
API addition documented in API changelog and SDK teams notified (resume_token, client_heartbeat headers)
Integration and load tests covering disconnect->resume and heavy stalled-client scenarios pass in CI

2026-03-10: QA found a race where aggressive mark-to-delete collided with concurrent resume; fixed by adding short advisory lock during state transition. Additional e2e tests added. (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8974)
Follow-ups: client SDK heartbeat backoff logic and dedicated tenant TTL overrides.

Log samples: include generation_id, tenant_id, endpoint, last_heartbeat_ts for fast triage

Full rollout 7d after stable canary or rollback immediately on threshold breach
Provide a customer toggle to extend STALE window for Dedicated/Private deployments
testing: Unit tests for lease transitions and resume token validation
Integration: simulate client disconnects at different intervals and assert GC outcomes
